According to the latest issue of the Power On newsletter, Apple was reportedly once considering adding a feature to its "Apple Upgrade" program that would make setting up an iPhone almost seamless: having Apple pre-copy a user's data onto the new device. However, the feature ultimately never came to fruition.

The concept is simple: if a user regularly upgrades through fixed monthly instalment payments, why not make the process of switching to a new phone as convenient as possible? Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman reports:

There are some obvious loopholes here. First of all, your iCloud backup will be slightly out of date, because data transfer can only happen at the time of shipment—a few days after the order date—unless you choose to pick it up in person at a store.

There's also an obvious privacy concern. That said, if you've been using iCloud backup all along, it shouldn't come as a surprise that Apple has your data. But the average user might worry about how the data gets to the new phone, and whether anyone handles it in the process.

Two years ago, Apple rolled out a brand-new system across its retail stores called "Presto," which allows staff to update an iPhone's software while it's still in the box. It's easy to imagine this system being expanded in the future to support iCloud backup transfers, with no one touching your data the entire time.

However, this feature ultimately never launched, and that might be a good thing.
